content.title: About
content.content: Grilled shrimp have a tender flesh, a light smoky aroma, and a naturally sweet flavor. They are high‑protein, low‑calorie, and provide essential minerals such as iodine, zinc, and selenium.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp belong to the crustacean family and are among the most consumed seafood worldwide.
Grilling preserves most nutrients while adding a distinctive charred flavor.
There are over 2,000 shrimp species, but tiger and white shrimp are most common in cuisine.
Shrimp can change shell color depending on water temperature and growth stage.
In Japan, grilled shrimp are often served with soy sauce and wasabi.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving of grilled shrimp provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: The same serving contains roughly 90 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly option.

items.title: Source of iodine
items.content: Iodine supports thyroid function and hormonal balance.

items.title: Contains omega‑3s
items.content: Shrimp supply modest amounts of EPA and DHA, beneficial for heart and brain health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Astaxanthin, present in shrimp, helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, requiring medical attention.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: In certain regions shrimp can accumulate cadmium or mercury, so choose reputable sources.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow bacterial growth leading to food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grilled shrimp can be enjoyed as a standalone appetizer, added to salads, pastas, rice dishes, or used in sandwiches. They are easy to eat with fingers, or can be sliced for incorporation into hot meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh shrimp in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for no more than 2 days. Frozen shrimp store at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen shrimp in the fridge before cooking, and store cooked grilled shrimp in an airtight container for no more than 24 hours.
